scope: Source comparison, preservation, binding publication and rollback of observed_revision2 only. archive65 and its two original ZIPs are historical baselines. Two directed RAM cases were executed separately against each revision; the65-test suite was inspected and not rerun.

findings.finding: Capture starts from a fresh, pinned actual startup and verifies all380 actual components, current owner lifetimes, original selected verifier and actual source map. It retains historical selected pins plus Native/operator/launcher closure and records unit source sets. Each runtime/installation source snapshot compares complete raw startup/UI hashes, full selected map and all declared components/immutable sources/unit files. There are no hardcoded old GTK/identity after-SHAs to restore. A later legitimate release causes HOLD/resealing rather than replacement by the captured release.

The actual new owner/config/native manifest is observed; original bootstrap provenance and original b77 metadata verifier are gates. make_binding deep-copies the currently selected document, retains every historical source entry and only adds the actual run config, refusing existing-path SHA conflict. Source count is dynamic. config_patch deep-copies the full latest captured UI/startup, changing only face_readback and its one existing component pin. Identity/gallery/model/TTL/clock/GTK/axis values and other component pins are retained. The complete source snapshot and original metadata verifier are repeated before known-byte UI/startup replacement.

Backups/intent are O_EXCL-created and fsynced before publication. replace_known rechecks exact expected bytes before temporary creation and before rename, then verifies readback. Rollback requires same boot/contract, normally inactive services and no hardware owners; it prevalidates both before/after backup hashes and the full live byte set plus active ledger before the first reversal. Newer identity/startup/UI or unrelated ledger bytes fail closed. Withdrawal removes only known own systemd files, keeps running entry/startup/selected bindings and retains package/state. It does not roll back Native state. This relies on the explicit freeze of external writers; rename is not a kernel conditional-rename primitive.

The intent seals prior_active_raw, but the final active-source update passes regular(active_path) freshly read at line593 as the CAS expected value. The immediate source recapture only requires startup/UI bytes to be unchanged. A newer, still-consistent ledger whose transaction metadata changed is accepted by the exact source_snapshot and overwritten, even though its SHA differs from intent.active_before_sha256. This weakens the claimed refusal of unexpected concurrent publication. Both exact revision-specific bind_camera methods returned COMMITTED in the targeted RAM case; that literal mocked outcome is not a real Native approval.
minimal_fix: Use captured prior ledger bytes and captured existence as the expected state. Do not accept a fresh regular(active_path) value as the publication CAS expectation.

Recheck the captured ledger/existence before the first UI/startup mutation, then replace_known(active_path, prior_active_raw, encoded(active)) if it originally existed; if originally absent, require absence and use O_EXCL create. An appeared/disappeared/changed ledger must HOLD. Prefer carrying the exact active raw bytes/existence from the initial source snapshot so one transaction has one expected ledger.

Keep the two directed cases: unchanged baseline commits; an intervening newer ledger must be rejected without overwriting it. With the pre-write guard, the injected change in this reproduction should also leave UI/startup untouched.
findings.risk_boundary: Unexpected writer or publication drift despite the operational writer freeze, not malicious-root authentication. No model/hardware consequence was simulated.

findings.finding: If a crash occurs after active-source is published but before committed.json creation, current rollback accepts neither the prior ledger nor missing committed(None), so it safely HOLDs before reversing any bytes. A single exact rollback RAM fault-state case confirmed NEWER_ACTIVE_LEDGER_CONFLICT and no mutation despite known UI/startup backups. The already-current bind branch returns before committed creation, so reentry does not complete that receipt. This is a documented manual-reconciliation/availability limit, not an unsafe automatic rollback or Native-state overwrite.
findings.minimal_recommendation: Either explicitly retain manual reconciliation for this phase in the rollback contract, or precompute and O_EXCL/fsync-seal active-source.after.json and its intent SHA before the first publication. Then rollback can recognize exact presealed before/after ledger bytes independently of whether the final committed marker was reached. Do not derive trusted after evidence from the current ledger alone or create Native receipts/markers.
findings.approval_effect: Not a second safety blocker if explicit manual reconciliation is accepted. It blocks a claim that automatic rollback covers every interruption point.

external_gates_remaining.required: Fresh merged dpu-auto-config.service body/DropInPaths/ExecStart and actual init/helper source pins plus reviewed ordering, or proven current not-found. The fresh explicit review flag and actual unit/source closure must remain mandatory. Historical unit listing, a nonempty arbitrary pin list or this static review does not fill this gate.

Explicit returned exclusive maintenance, fresh actual boot/startup/380/selected/owner metadata, genuine original stop/full-history receipt where applicable, actual target graph/merged properties and one original cold-start Native/GUI READY acceptance. No source/seed/marker may be fabricated.

conditional_approval: Source preservation, selected projection, known UI/startup-byte publication and guarded rollback are acceptable for offline review. Unconditional CAS approval is withheld until the active-ledger expectation is fixed and the directed case is rejected. After that, refreshed revision-specific validation/ZIP evidence and all fresh external gates still precede installation or cold-boot acceptance.
